text: Of the many, many things we’re not supposed to snack on, perhaps the most common forbidden
ipa: /ˈʌv ðə mˈɛni mˈɛni θˈɪŋz wˈɝ nˈɑt səpˈoʊzd tˈu snˈæk ˈɑn pɚhˈæps ðə mˈoʊst kˈɑmən fˈɔɹbɪdən/
vi: Trong số rất nhiều thứ chúng ta không được phép ăn vặt, có lẽ thứ bị cấm phổ biến nhất

text: food is silica gel.
ipa: /fˈud ˈɪz sˈɪləkə dʒˈɛl/

text: This tiny packet pops up in packaging for everything— from TVs
ipa: /ðˈɪs tˈaɪni pˈækət pˈɑps ˈʌp ɪn pˈækɪdʒɪŋ fˈɔɹ ˈɛvɹiθˌɪŋ fɹˈʌm tˈivˈiz/

text: and guitar cases to sunscreen and snack foods.
ipa: /ənd ɡɪtˈɑɹ kˈeɪsəz tˈu sənskɹˈin ənd snˈæk fˈudz/

text: So why is silica gel everywhere, and what would actually happen if you ate
ipa: /sˈoʊ wˈaɪ ˈɪz sˈɪləkə dʒˈɛl ˈɛvɹiwˌɛɹ ənd wˈʌt wˈʊd ˈæktʃˌuəli hˈæpən ˈɪf jˈu ˈeɪt/

text: it? Found in the Earth’s crust, silica, also called silicon dioxide, is typically mined
ipa: /ˈɪt fˈaʊnd ɪn ðə ˈɝθs kɹˈʌst sˈɪləkə ˈɔlsoʊ kˈɔld sˈɪləkən daɪˈɑksˌaɪd ˈɪz tˈɪpɪkli mˈaɪnd/

text: as raw silica sand, which is then washed, dried, sifted, and chemically treated.
ipa: /ˈæz ɹˈɑ sˈɪləkə sˈænd wˈɪtʃ ˈɪz ðˈɛn wˈɑʃt dɹˈaɪd sˈɪftɪd ənd kˈɛməkli tɹˈitɪd/

text: Once manufacturers ensure each grain is uniform, the processed sand gets mixed with sodium carbonate,
ipa: /wˈʌns mˌænjəfˈæktʃɚɚz ɛnʃˈʊɹ ˈitʃ ɡɹˈeɪn ˈɪz jˈunəfˌɔɹm ðə pɹˈɑsɛst sˈænd ɡˈɛts mˈɪkst wˈɪð sˈoʊdiəm kˈɑɹbənˌeɪt/

text: then heated and combined with an acid that links the silica particles into a jelly-like matrix.
ipa: /ðˈɛn hˈitəd ənd kəmbˈaɪnd wˈɪð ˈæn ˈæsəd ðˈæt lˈɪŋks ðə sˈɪləkə pˈɑɹtəkəlz ˈɪntu ə jellylike mˈeɪtɹɪks/

text: This matrix gives the material its porous structure, which stays stable
ipa: /ðˈɪs mˈeɪtɹɪks ɡˈɪvz ðə mətˈɪɹiəl ˈɪts pˈɔɹəs stɹˈʌktʃɚ wˈɪtʃ stˈeɪz stˈeɪbəl/

text: after being washed and dried into hard, glassy beads.
ipa: /ˈæftɚ bˈiɪŋ wˈɑʃt ənd dɹˈaɪd ˈɪntu hˈɑɹd ɡlˈæsi bˈidz/

text: The final product is chemically identical to the sand you might find on a beach—
ipa: /ðə fˈaɪnəl pɹˈɑdəkt ˈɪz kˈɛməkli aɪdˈɛntɪkəl tˈu ðə sˈænd jˈu mˈaɪt fˈaɪnd ˈɑn ə bˈitʃ/

text: the only difference is that porous structure.
ipa: /ðə ˈoʊnli dˈɪfɚəns ˈɪz ðˈæt pˈɔɹəs stɹˈʌktʃɚ/

text: Inside each silica gel bead is a massive microscopic network of tunnels.
ipa: /ˌɪnsˈaɪd ˈitʃ sˈɪləkə dʒˈɛl bˈid ˈɪz ə mˈæsɪv mˌaɪkɹəskˈɑpɪk nˈɛtwˌɝk ˈʌv tˈʌnəlz/

text: This dramatically increases the surface area of each bead, with a single gram of silica offering
ipa: /ðˈɪs dɹəmˈætɪkli ɪnkɹˈisəz ðə sˈɝfəs ˈɛɹiə ˈʌv ˈitʃ bˈid wˈɪð ə sˈɪŋɡəl ɡɹˈæm ˈʌv sˈɪləkə ˈɔfɚɪŋ/

text: over 700 square meters of surface area.
ipa: /ˈoʊvɚ 700 skwˈɛɹ mˈitɚz ˈʌv sˈɝfəs ˈɛɹiə/

text: But this space doesn’t stay empty for long.
ipa: /bˈʌt ðˈɪs spˈeɪs doesnt stˈeɪ ˈɛmpti fˈɔɹ lˈɔŋ/

text: The silicon dioxide molecules that make up the gel are held together by polar covalent bonds,
ipa: /ðə sˈɪləkən daɪˈɑksˌaɪd mˈɑləkjˌulz ðˈæt mˈeɪk ˈʌp ðə dʒˈɛl ˈɑɹ hˈɛld təɡˈɛðɚ bˈaɪ pˈoʊlɚ koʊvˈɑlənt bˈɑndz/

text: which attract other polar substances, including water.
ipa: /wˈɪtʃ ətɹˈækt ˈʌðɚ pˈoʊlɚ sˈʌbstənsəz ˌɪnklˈudɪŋ wˈɔtɚ/

text: So when silica gel is placed in a humid environment, the water in the air
ipa: /sˈoʊ wˈɛn sˈɪləkə dʒˈɛl ˈɪz plˈeɪst ɪn ə hjˈuməd ɪnvˈaɪɹənmənt ðə wˈɔtɚ ɪn ðə ˈɛɹ/

text: is drawn to the beads’ surface.
ipa: /ˈɪz dɹˈɔn tˈu ðə bˈidz sˈɝfəs/

text: From these surface pores, the water vapor
ipa: /fɹˈʌm ðˈiz sˈɝfəs pˈɔɹz ðə wˈɔtɚ vˈeɪpɚ/

text: is then pulled inside the grain through a process called capillary condensation.
ipa: /ˈɪz ðˈɛn pˈʊld ˌɪnsˈaɪd ðə ɡɹˈeɪn θɹˈu ə pɹˈɑsˌɛs kˈɔld kˈæpəlˌɛɹi kˌɑndənsˈeɪʃən/

text: Each grain can hold up to 40% of its own weight in water, allowing a standard
ipa: /ˈitʃ ɡɹˈeɪn kˈæn hˈoʊld ˈʌp tˈu 40 ˈʌv ˈɪts ˈoʊn wˈeɪt ɪn wˈɔtɚ əlˈaʊɪŋ ə stˈændɚd/

text: 5-gram packet to hold roughly 2 grams of liquid.
ipa: /5gram pˈækət tˈu hˈoʊld ɹˈʌfli 2 ɡɹˈæmz ˈʌv lˈɪkwəd/

text: And since this liquid is held inside the bead’s internal network, even fully saturated silica doesn't
ipa: /ənd sˈɪns ðˈɪs lˈɪkwəd ˈɪz hˈɛld ˌɪnsˈaɪd ðə bˈidz ˌɪntˈɝnəl nˈɛtwˌɝk ˈivɪn fˈʊli sˈætʃɚˌeɪtɪd sˈɪləkə dˈʌzənt/

text: feel wet to the touch.
ipa: /fˈil wˈɛt tˈu ðə tˈʌtʃ/

text: This ability makes silica gel a desiccant, a type of substance used to keep things dry.
ipa: /ðˈɪs əbˈɪlətˌi mˈeɪks sˈɪləkə dʒˈɛl ə desiccant ə tˈaɪp ˈʌv sˈʌbstəns jˈuzd tˈu kˈip θˈɪŋz dɹˈaɪ/

text: But these beads can suck up more than just water.
ipa: /bˈʌt ðˈiz bˈidz kˈæn sˈʌk ˈʌp mˈɔɹ ðˈæn dʒˈʌst wˈɔtɚ/

text: Silica attracts ammonia, sulfur dioxide, and a handful of other gases, making it useful in gas
ipa: /sˈɪləkə ətɹˈækts əmˈoʊnjə sˈʌlfɚ daɪˈɑksˌaɪd ənd ə hˈændfˌʊl ˈʌv ˈʌðɚ ɡˈæsəz mˈeɪkɪŋ ˈɪt jˈusfəl ɪn ɡˈæs/

text: masks and other filtration systems.
ipa: /mˈæsks ənd ˈʌðɚ fɪltɹˈeɪʃən sˈɪstəmz/

text: The pace of this process depends on the environment.
ipa: /ðə pˈeɪs ˈʌv ðˈɪs pɹˈɑsˌɛs dɪpˈɛndz ˈɑn ðə ɪnvˈaɪɹənmənt/

text: In a very humid enclosed space, a packet could reach its saturation point within a day
ipa: /ɪn ə vˈɛɹi hjˈuməd ɛnklˈoʊzd spˈeɪs ə pˈækət kˈʊd ɹˈitʃ ˈɪts sˌætʃɚˈeɪʃən pˈɔɪnt wɪðˈɪn ə dˈeɪ/

text: or two, but this could take up to a week in a moderately humid environment.
ipa: /ˈɔɹ tˈu bˈʌt ðˈɪs kˈʊd tˈeɪk ˈʌp tˈu ə wˈik ɪn ə mˈɑdɚətli hjˈuməd ɪnvˈaɪɹənmənt/

text: Either way, silica gel beads functionally last forever
ipa: /ˈiðɚ wˈeɪ sˈɪləkə dʒˈɛl bˈidz fˈʌŋkʃənəli lˈæst fɚˈɛvɚ/

text: since you can dry them out in a hot oven.
ipa: /sˈɪns jˈu kˈæn dɹˈaɪ ðˈɛm ˈaʊt ɪn ə hˈɑt ˈʌvən/

text: These abilities and silica’s prevalence in Earth’s crust have made it the planet’s most popular commercial
ipa: /ðˈiz əbˈɪlətˌiz ənd silicas pɹˈɛvələns ɪn ˈɝθs kɹˈʌst hˈæv mˈeɪd ˈɪt ðə plˈænəts mˈoʊst pˈɑpjəlɚ kəmˈɝʃəl/

text: desiccant since we started mass producing it in 1919.
ipa: /desiccant sˈɪns wˈi stˈɑɹtɪd mˈæs pɹədˈusɪŋ ˈɪt ɪn 1919/

text: At home, it keeps snacks crispy and extends their shelf life, ensures pills
ipa: /ˈæt hˈoʊm ˈɪt kˈips snˈæks kɹˈɪspi ənd ɪkstˈɛndz ðˈɛɹ ʃˈɛlf lˈaɪf ɛnʃˈʊɹz pˈɪlz/

text: and vitamins stay dry, and captures any stinky scents from your cat’s litter box.
ipa: /ənd vˈaɪtəmənz stˈeɪ dɹˈaɪ ənd kˈæptʃɚz ˈɛni stˈɪŋki sˈɛnts fɹˈʌm jˈɔɹ kˈæts lˈɪtɚ bˈɑks/

text: Museums use silica gel in exhibit cases to prevent metal artifacts from rusting
ipa: /mjuzˈiəmz jˈus sˈɪləkə dʒˈɛl ɪn ɪɡzˈɪbɪt kˈeɪsəz tˈu pɹɪvˈɛnt mˈɛtəl ˈɑɹtəfˌækts fɹˈʌm ɹˈʌstɪŋ/

text: and preserved animals from growing mold.
ipa: /ənd pɹəzˈɝvd ˈænəməlz fɹˈʌm ɡɹˈoʊɪŋ mˈoʊld/

text: And in outer space, a form of silica gel called aerogel is used to insulate rovers
ipa: /ənd ɪn ˈaʊtɚ spˈeɪs ə fˈɔɹm ˈʌv sˈɪləkə dʒˈɛl kˈɔld aerogel ˈɪz jˈuzd tˈu ˈɪnsəlˌeɪt ɹˈoʊvɚz/

text: from extreme temperatures and capture high-velocity comet dust for study back home.
ipa: /fɹˈʌm ɛkstɹˈim tˈɛmpɹətʃɚz ənd kˈæptʃɚ highvelocity kˈɑmət dˈʌst fˈɔɹ stˈʌdi bˈæk hˈoʊm/

text: But what about what silica gel would do to you if you successfully swallowed a packet?
ipa: /bˈʌt wˈʌt əbˈaʊt wˈʌt sˈɪləkə dʒˈɛl wˈʊd dˈu tˈu jˈu ˈɪf jˈu səksˈɛsfəli swˈɑloʊd ə pˈækət/

text: The answer is... not much.
ipa: /ðə ˈænsɚ ˈɪz nˈɑt mˈʌtʃ/

text: Those “Do Not Eat” warnings have more to do with packets being choking hazards
ipa: /ðˈoʊz dˈu nˈɑt ˈit wˈɔɹnɪŋz hˈæv mˈɔɹ tˈu dˈu wˈɪð pˈækɪts bˈiɪŋ tʃˈoʊkɪŋ hˈæzɚdz/

text: than any silica-specific concerns.
ipa: /ðˈæn ˈɛni silicaspecific kənsˈɝnz/

text: Besides, your body has so much liquid in it— even
ipa: /bɪsˈaɪdz jˈɔɹ bˈɑdi hˈæz sˈoʊ mˈʌtʃ lˈɪkwəd ɪn ˈɪt ˈivɪn/

text: if the packet did suck up the standard 2 grams, you could replenish
ipa: /ˈɪf ðə pˈækət dˈɪd sˈʌk ˈʌp ðə stˈændɚd 2 ɡɹˈæmz jˈu kˈʊd ɹiplˈɛnɪʃ/

text: that much and more with a single glass of water.
ipa: /ðˈæt mˈʌtʃ ənd mˈɔɹ wˈɪð ə sˈɪŋɡəl ɡlˈæs ˈʌv wˈɔtɚ/

text: And since silica is chemically inert, your body won’t break the gel down into something toxic.
ipa: /ənd sˈɪns sˈɪləkə ˈɪz kˈɛməkli ˌɪnˈɝt jˈɔɹ bˈɑdi wˈoʊnt bɹˈeɪk ðə dʒˈɛl dˈaʊn ˈɪntu sˈʌmθɪŋ tˈɑksɪk/

text: That said, downing larger quantities of silica gel would be unpleasant.
ipa: /ðˈæt sˈɛd dˈaʊnɪŋ lˈɑɹdʒɚ kwˈɑntətiz ˈʌv sˈɪləkə dʒˈɛl wˈʊd bˈi ənplˈɛzənt/

text: Its moisture-wicking properties could dry and irritate mucous membranes along the digestive tract, resulting in diarrhea
ipa: /ˈɪts moisturewicking pɹˈɑpɚtiz kˈʊd dɹˈaɪ ənd ˈɪɹɪtˌeɪt mjˈukəs mˈɛmbɹˌeɪnz əlˈɔŋ ðə daɪdʒˈɛstɪv tɹˈækt ɹɪzˈʌltɪŋ ɪn dˌaɪɚˈiə/

text: and an upset stomach.
ipa: /ənd ˈæn əpsˈɛt stˈʌmək/

text: Worse still, some silica is coated with cobalt chloride to indicate moisture levels,
ipa: /wˈɝs stˈɪl sˈʌm sˈɪləkə ˈɪz kˈoʊtəd wˈɪð kˈoʊbˌɔlt klˈɔɹaɪd tˈu ˈɪndəkˌeɪt mˈɔɪstʃɚ lˈɛvəlz/

text: and that compound actually is toxic.
ipa: /ənd ðˈæt kˈɑmpaʊnd ˈæktʃˌuəli ˈɪz tˈɑksɪk/

text: But assuming your silica snack is of the standard variety, you should survive the ordeal.
ipa: /bˈʌt əsˈumɪŋ jˈɔɹ sˈɪləkə snˈæk ˈɪz ˈʌv ðə stˈændɚd vɚˈaɪəti jˈu ʃˈʊd sɚvˈaɪv ðə ɔɹdˈil/
